paper.title_en: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
paper.abstract_en: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. In this work, two novel DePFET technologies that address the two factors of the signal-to-noise ratio through fundamental changes to the intrinsic design are characterised: a buried-channel design aimed at reducing the limiting low-frequency noise by weakening the coupling between the channel and Si/SiO$_2$ interface traps, and a super-$g_q$ design intended to increase the charge gain by reducing the effective internal-gate capacitance. Their noise and energy resolution were mapped across the transistor bias space, over a wide temperature range (100-260 K) and for integration times of 0.4-9 $μ$s (readout times of 2-19.2 $μ$s per row), and compared with standard DePFETs as developed for the NewAthena Wide Field Imager (WFI). All three variants reach their lowest noise at about 155 K. The buried-channel device achieves an excellent equivalent noise charge (ENC) of 0.96 e$^-$ (at most 0.83 e$^-$ after subtracting the readout-electronics noise), demonstrating sub-electron noise over a complete 64$\times$64 DePFET matrix in a single readout, alongside a power consumption reduction of more than 50%. The super-$g_q$ DePFET shows a 2.6-fold increase in charge gain (about 1100 pA/e$^-$) but exhibits higher total noise due to an excess noise contribution. The results highlight the potential of the novel DePFETs, with the buried-channel technology offering immediate benefits for low-noise applications such as the WFI.
